items.title: Eddie Marshall interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: anyone knows what that sound is on the piano, it’s Hank Jones. Everybody knows that.

ctx.x: Right. It’s not just a musical issue.

Right. Because when it gets down to that level, I don’t have any greater pleasure than I did playing with my kids. It never gets that relaxed, playing with anybody. Because we’ve just done it so often and it’s been so real and so — you know they’re your kids. So it’s a different thing. Now I played like last night, I played with this wonderful kid, Leonard Thompson. These kids, I mean I could be their grandfather actually. These kids © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-

are maybe like 25, 30 years old, something like that. Really a great player. And the same with Jon, who is an Asian kid. But the thing is you can always tell when you’re playing with any musician, you can hear, with the piano player, the sound that he gets on the piano. Like most of these kids, well most young musicians, it might be a lot of flash and everything because a lot of young kids can do that. But there’s a sound that a jazz pianist emits and a feeling. And I always have to — what is that sound exactly?…
